label: Stage 2 -- collapse vs box precision at ONE config (8px deployed, 108 val tiles)
verdict: NO SIGN FLIP -- the box-robustness hypothesis is NOT supported
reading: beta=0 -> beta=0.5 raises mean crown IoU by +0.0483 with PERFECT boxes and +0.0476 with PREDICTED boxes -- the same benefit to within 0.0007. Collapse helps by an amount independent of box precision, so it does not buy box-robustness. The apparent sign flip in the prior evidence was a STRIDE/STACK artefact: the GT-box arm showing collapse hurting (masker_lab, crown IoU 0.7412 -> 0.6590) is 16px/local, while the deployed config is 8px/Modal. Note beta=0 scores nearly identically at both strides (0.7402 here vs 0.7412 in the lab); it is beta=0.5 that differs (0.7885 vs 0.6590).
reproduction_gate: b05_pred_all reproduces the recorded val cell EXACTLY: AP50 0.6392 and mAP50-95 0.2680 vs sweep_val_knobs_s0.json (alpha=0.3, kappa=1.6, thr=0.25) 0.6392 / 0.2680. The new box-source eval path is scoring identically to the published one.
what_survives: Collapse is beneficial at the deployed 8px config regardless of box precision, and (Stage 1) the mixture reduces to K=2 with no change. What is NOT supported is any claim that the benefit comes from robustness to imprecise boxes. Whether the 16px-vs-8px reversal is caused by stride or by the local/Modal stack is untested and confounded.
